notes: Windows: a file the app refuses to open no longer ends in an error. When Windows cannot open a file at all (a format it cannot decode, or a container such as TS or AVI), the app now converts it as it plays instead of stopping with a 3016 error; direct links without a file extension get the same treatment. When a stream really cannot play, the message says what happened: the host answered 403, or sent a page instead of the video. Earlier: files with Dolby Digital, Dolby Digital Plus, DTS or TrueHD audio play with sound, video the machine cannot decode is converted, and the file's languages are listed under Audio.
